title: Two-photon microscopy and spectral detection for ex vivo imaging of individual stem cells
protocol: Cover an open objective position with lens paper.
Tune NIR laser to a wavelength visible by human eye (e.g., 720nm).
Select fiber-coupled laser line (e.g., 561nm) and appropriate main dichroic (e.g., HFT KP 700/561).
Choose high zoom settings and start scanning.
Adjust laser power until a dark red spot (e.g., 720nm) and a spot in the color of the fiber-coupled laser line are visible on the lens paper.
Adjust one mirror until both spots are centered to each other.
Switch to a low magnification objective and image the alignment slide in reflected light with both laser lines in two channels simultaneously.
Adjust the second mirror until both images overlap.
Repeat steps 6 to 8 until the two laser lines overlap perfectly in the back-aperture and focal plane.
Use laser spectrum analyzer and test sample to check quality of NIR laser.
Place cover-slip next to output beam aperture of NIR laser.
Place the input window of the spectrometer head into the dimmer beam. If signal is too high, place a piece of Scott-tape in front of it.
Tune spectrometer to wavelength selected for NIR laser.
You should see a stable, bell-shaped spectral curve.
Harvest bone marrow cells from actin-eGFP transgenic mice.
Isolate HCSs using FACS1.
Inject cells into tail vein of mouse.
Sacrifice mouse.
Isolate femur and tibia.
Remove muscle.
Cut bone into 2-3mm thick pieces in vertical orientation using a small saw.
Fill Petri dish with 2mm of 0.5% agarose in PBS.
Insert bone into the agarose layer of the Petri dish with open end toward the dish bottom as close as possible to cover-slip.
Add DMEM.
Switch on heating of incubator box.
Tune NIR laser to 920 nm to image eGFP.
Decide on objective lens to be used for experiment.
Set up beam-path of two-photon microscope to image eGFP labeled cells.
Image eGFP labeled cell using these settings.
Set up beam-path of two-photon microscope for spectral imaging of eGFP labeled cells for reference spectrum.
Acquire reference spectrum from eGFP labeled cell and save it.
Replace slide with eGFP labeled cells with Petri-dish containing live bone fragments.
Set up microscope for wide-field DIC imaging.
Remove plastic lid of Petri dish when using DIC.
Find bone fragments, focusing on the center where it appears reddish in transmitted light.
Set up beam-path of two-photon microscope to image eGFP, SHG and transmitted light DIC.
Image sample until a potential cell is found.
Set up beam-path of two-photon microscope for spectral detection.
Compare spectrum to reference spectrum of eGFP.
Ensure the spectrum of an eGFP labeled cell (peak at 507nm) is identical to the reference spectrum.
Repeat steps 34 to 37 until eGFP positive cell is identified.
Switch back to settings established in step 34 if cell was positively identified.
Select time interval for time-lapse imaging, such as 15 minutes.
Set up z-stack if 3D imaging is required.
Start time-lapse imaging.
Set up beam-path of two-photon microscope for spectral detection and confirm identity of eGFP labeled cells.
Move on to next cell and repeat previous steps starting at step 34.
Remove noise with 3x3 median filter using standard image acquisition software.
Load results into 3D software if z-stacks were acquired in steps 41 and 42.
Identify cells of interest and define cell volume if z-stack was set up.
Subtract background from eGFP signal if z-stack was set up.
Identify cells of interest using transmitted light DIC and all fluorescence channels if quantification is required.
Define cell volume based on second label if quantification is required.
Subtract background from signal if quantification is required.
Measure corrected mean intensity of signal label within cell volume defined by second label if quantification is required.
Load image at single time point into ImageJ.
Measure background and define threshold, for example 90% to 120% of mean background intensity.
Set pixels below threshold to zero.
Draw segmented line along bone surface.
Start Java custom script.
Sample intensities along the line.
For each sample point on the line, calculate mean intensities of all pixels within ±8 µm perpendicular to the line.
Divide the number of pixels along the line that have intensity greater than the threshold by the total number of pixels.
Optional: Repeat steps 49 to 52 for second color if multicolor co-localization is required.
To estimate co-localization, count all pixels along the line with mean intensity values larger than the threshold in both channels.
Divide this number by the total number of pixels along the line.
